title: PainMap pain-driver context datasets
purpose: Expose additional source-backed evidence relevant to identifying major causes of pain by place without collapsing incompatible evidence into one score.

comparison_policy.reason: Mortality rates, animal counts, insecticide mass, and land area use incompatible units and represent different causal and evidential relationships to pain.
allowed: Within-place comparison among the four human mortality-rate indicators, which share deaths per 100,000 population.
Within-metric comparison across places when method, unit, and reference-period semantics match.

datasets.label: Human mortality-linked pain-driver context
indicators: mortality attributed to household and ambient air pollution
mortality attributed to unsafe water, sanitation and hygiene
datasets.attribution: World Health Organization, via World Bank Indicators API
datasets.caveat: Mortality is a severe-outcome context proxy. It does not measure pain intensity, duration, prevalence, disability, nonfatal suffering, or total welfare burden.

datasets.label: Source-backed animal, insecticide, and land context
datasets.caveat: These rows are public candidate context, not canonical PainMap measurements. Land area is a denominator, not a cause of pain, and is excluded from cause rankings.
